chunks: From him, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about fish found floating on the water or thrown up by the sea dead; should one eat it? He said, 'No.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat fish found dead floating on the water according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that fish found floating or washed ashore dead are impermissible, establishing the principle that 'death by water' requires the animal to be alive at the moment of death for consumption. This ruling distinguishes Shia jurisprudence from some Sunni schools that permit all sea creatures, emphasizing the necessity of a living state prior to death for aquatic animals. The narration highlights the scholarly focus on the method of death as a critical factor in determining the purity and permissibility of seafood.
